constraints: New files only: scripts/code_map/build.py (a build(root, *, artifacts=None, out=None) -> int plain-importable seam wrapping the same extract/render calls cli._build makes -- cli._build refactored to call it, one build path not two), scripts/code_map/precommit.py (the mechanism), scripts/hooks/code_map_precommit.py (the fail-open shim). Zero changes to scripts/code_map/discovery.py, extract.py, render.py internals, and zero changes to tests/test_code_map.py's existing content (MapTreeFreshnessTests stays byte-identical -- hard constraint).

Mechanism, exact specification (resolves PLAN_CRITIC.md findings 2-4,7-9): (1) opportunistically run `git worktree prune` first to self-heal any admin residue from a prior crashed run; (2) snapshot the INDEX (not the working tree) via `git write-tree` -> `git commit-tree <tree> -p HEAD -m <marker>` (a dangling, non-ref-touching commit) -> `git worktree add --detach <unique-path> <that commit>`, where <unique-path> comes from `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='code-map-precommit-')` every invocation (never a fixed name -- this is what makes two concurrent invocations from sibling worktrees collision-free, since each gets a distinct admin entry); (3) run build() against that ephemeral worktree; (4) copy-back is PLAIN FILE I/O, not git plumbing -- read the built map/INDEX.md and map/ids.jsonl bytes from the ephemeral worktree, write those bytes to the same two paths in the REAL working tree (the repo_root resolved via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from cwd at hook run time -- dynamic per invoking worktree, never a path baked in at install time, so a hook shared across sibling worktrees on different branches always resolves and imports each worktree's OWN copy of this module), compare against the staged blobs (`git show :map/INDEX.md`, `git show :map/ids.jsonl`) to decide which of the two actually changed; (5) `git add -- map/INDEX.md map/ids.jsonl` in the real repo naming only the paths that changed (never a directory/glob add, never touching any other path) -- this is what makes 'exactly two paths, never an unrelated file' true by construction, since no step ever writes or adds any other path; (6) remove the ephemeral worktree (`git worktree remove --force <unique-path>`) in a `finally` block INSIDE the outer try/except, so cleanup runs on every path including fail-open, and a cleanup failure is itself swallowed and logged, never allowed to propagate.

Timeout, exact specification (resolves PLAN_CRITIC.md finding 3, the sharpest gap): every subprocess call in the mechanism (write-tree, commit-tree, worktree add, the build call, worktree remove, worktree prune) passes an explicit timeout= to subprocess.run (10 seconds each -- roughly 3x the measured 2.9s build baseline). A subprocess.TimeoutExpired is caught by the SAME outer try/except boundary as any other exception and results in the same fail-open exit 0 -- a hang must never block the commit any more than a crash does.

Fail-open contract, exact specification (resolves PLAN_CRITIC.md finding 9): the shim's entire body (including the finally-block cleanup) is wrapped in one broad try/except Exception; ANY exception, including subprocess.TimeoutExpired, results in exit 0. On every fail-open exit, print exactly one diagnostic line to stderr naming what was swallowed (git shows hook stderr on a normal commit without failing it -- zero UX cost, and it is the only signal against this mechanism regressing to a silent dead hook, which is precisely the human-process failure mode this mission exists to close). On the success (no staleness) path, print nothing. On the fixed-staleness path, print one line naming the two paths staged.

Auditable-boundary and partial-commit test coverage required in tests/test_code_map_precommit.py (new file, disposable scratch git repos under tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() only -- never this repo's own git state): fresh/no-op (map already matches the index, no stage, git status clean after); stale/rebuild-and-stage (source change staged, hook rebuilds+stages exactly the two paths); pathspec-restricted partial commit (two tracked files change, only one staged via `git add <one>`, then the mechanism is called directly -- built map reflects only the staged file's effect, unstaged sibling untouched); hunk-restricted partial commit (one file two hunks, only one staged via `git apply --cached`, the same net index state `git commit -p` produces -- built map excludes the unstaged hunk's effect); unrelated-dirty-file audit (a third tracked file dirty, staged or unstaged, present throughout -- `git diff --cached --name-only` after the mechanism runs is exactly {map/INDEX.md, map/ids.jsonl} or a subset, never includes the third file); concurrent-invocation (two mechanism calls launched against clones/worktrees of the same scratch repo at effectively the same time, e.g. via threading -- both complete successfully, no `git worktree add` collision, `git worktree list` shows zero residue afterward from either); forced-timeout (a fake runner that sleeps past the timeout on one subprocess call -- shim still exits 0 within a bounded wall-clock window, e.g. under 15s); forced-exception (a fake runner that raises -- shim exits 0, working tree otherwise unmodified, zero worktree/dangling-commit residue); worktree-run-time-resolution (invoke the shim from a second worktree of the scratch repo whose checkout predates this feature, i.e. lacks scripts/code_map/precommit.py at that commit -- shim still exits 0, fail-open covers the ImportError cleanly).
Stdlib only -- no new third-party dependency (matches scripts/code_map's own existing constraint).

Honest-Null escape hatch: if the concurrent-invocation test or the forced-timeout test cannot be made to pass with the pinned mechanism above (e.g. unique tempfile paths still collide under real concurrent load, or the timeout does not actually bound a real git-level hang), stop implementation and return-and-query the Commander with the negative evidence attached -- do not ship a hook whose own tests demonstrate it can corrupt state or hang under load. Per the Honest-Null Clause this is a complete, successful deliverable if it occurs; it has not been observed in either candidate's investigation, so it is a contingency, not the expected outcome.
File ownership: scripts/code_map/ (new files + cli._build refactor only, no other internals), scripts/hooks/, tests/. Nothing outside those touched.
